answer: A mechanism that actually bites: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because onyx only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, velvet is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any ripple approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
